items.title: Student visa for courses longer than 6 months
items.title_it: Student visa per corsi di oltre 6 mesi

other: Not needed by Irish citizens (Common Travel Area) or by EU/EEA/Swiss citizens who hold settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
Since 2021 this applies to EU/EEA/Swiss citizens without EUSS status too
Requires an offer from a licensed student sponsor

items.summary: You need an offer from a licensed student sponsor, enough money for the course and living costs, and English at the required level. Apply up to 6 months before the course starts from outside the UK (decision usually about 3 weeks). The healthcare surcharge is paid on top of the visa fee.
steps: Get an unconditional offer and a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from the university
Apply online up to 6 months before the course start and pay the fee plus the Immigration Health Surcharge
items.deadline: Earliest 6 months before the course starts (from outside the UK); from inside the UK up to 3 months before, and before the current visa expires

items.title: Student visa: money you must show
items.title_it: Student visa: fondi da dimostrare

other: Student visa applicants only
Exempt if you have lived in the UK on a valid visa for at least 12 months before applying

items.summary: Besides one year of course fees (as shown on the CAS), you must show living costs of £1,529/month in London or £1,171/month elsewhere, for up to 9 months. The money must have been held for 28 consecutive days, ending within 31 days of the application.
items.cost: Living costs: £1,529/month London, £1,171/month outside London, max 9 months (2026)
items.notes: London = City of London and the 32 London boroughs. Some nationalities on the 'differential evidence requirement' list may not need to submit the evidence upfront but can be asked for it.

items.title: Short courses (up to 6 months) as a Standard Visitor
items.title_it: Corsi brevi (fino a 6 mesi) come Standard Visitor

other: Not relevant for Irish citizens or EUSS status holders
Course at an accredited UK institution

items.summary: You can study for up to 6 months as a visitor at an accredited UK institution. Visitors cannot do paid or unpaid work and cannot claim benefits. Depending on nationality you need a visitor visa, an ETA, or nothing; most European nationals need an ETA.
items.cost: No visa fee if you only need an ETA (ETA £20)
items.notes: No Immigration Health Surcharge for stays of 6 months or less; NHS hospital care may be charged unless you have an EHIC (see gb-nhs-short-stay).

items.title: Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA)
items.title_it: Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA)

other: Usually needed by nationals of European countries, the USA, Canada, Australia and others who do not need a visa
Not needed with a British or Irish passport, or if you already have UK permission to live, work or study (e.g. Student visa, EUSS status)

items.summary: Most European visitors need an ETA rather than a visa to enter the UK for up to 6 months. Each traveller needs their own ETA.
items.notes: How many years one ETA stays valid is not stated on the pages read. Check the exact nationality rule with the gov.uk 'check if you need a UK visa' tool.

items.title: EU Settlement Scheme (settled / pre-settled status)
items.title_it: EU Settlement Scheme (settled / pre-settled status)

applies_to.residence_requirement: Living in the UK by 31 December 2020, or a joining family member of such a person
other: Main deadline was 30 June 2021; later applications only in specific cases (joining family members, reasonable grounds)
Not available to EU students who first moved to the UK after 2020: they need a Student visa

items.summary: EU/EEA/Swiss citizens living in the UK by the end of 2020 (and their joining family members) could apply for settled status (usually after 5 years of residence) or pre-settled status. Either status lets you work, study and use the NHS. Pre-settled status is lost after more than 5 consecutive years outside the UK (4 for Swiss citizens).
items.notes: EUSS status decides home fee status and student finance eligibility (see subsidies.json). Pre-settled status is extended by 5 years before it expires and may convert automatically to settled status.

items.title: Irish citizens: no visa or permission needed (Common Travel Area)
items.title_it: Cittadini irlandesi: nessun visto o permesso (Common Travel Area)

other: Irish citizens only

items.summary: Irish citizens do not need permission to enter or live in the UK. They can work (including self-employed), study at all levels on the same basis as UK citizens, use healthcare and access social security. They do not need to apply to the EU Settlement Scheme.

items.title: Graduate visa (staying to work after your degree)
items.title_it: Graduate visa (restare a lavorare dopo la laurea)

other: Must be in the UK on a Student (or Tier 4) visa and have completed an eligible course
Not needed by Irish citizens or EUSS status holders

items.summary: After finishing an eligible UK degree on a Student visa you can apply to stay and work in most jobs. Length: 2 years if you apply on or before 31 December 2026, 18 months if you apply on or after 1 January 2027, 3 years after a PhD.
items.deadline: Apply before your Student visa expires
items.cost: £937 fee + Immigration Health Surcharge, usually £1,035 per year (2026)

items.title: National Insurance number
items.title_it: National Insurance number (codice previdenziale/fiscale)

other: Needed if you work; you must live in the UK and have the right to work
Student visa holders may already have it on their BRP or eVisa (UKVI account)

items.summary: The National Insurance number is the UK number used for work, tax and contributions. Apply online once you are in the UK and have the right to work; you can start working before it arrives if you can prove your right to work.
steps: Check your eVisa (UKVI account) or BRP: you may already have one
Apply online from inside the UK with your passport or EU/EEA/Swiss ID card and prove your identity
Wait up to 4 weeks after identity is proved
items.cost: No fee mentioned on the official page
items.authority: HM Revenue & Customs / Department for Work and Pensions

items.title: Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) for Student visa holders
items.title_it: Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) per chi ha lo Student visa

other: Student visa applicants (EU/EEA/Swiss citizens without EUSS status included)

items.summary: Student visa applicants pay the IHS upfront for the whole visa. It gives NHS hospital care much like a resident, though some charges such as prescriptions or dental can still apply. Over 6 months and up to a year counts as a full year; partial extra years over 6 months are charged as half a year.
items.cost: £776 per year for students (2026); 18 months or less = £1,164
items.notes: Full-time EU/EEA/Swiss students with an EHIC who do not work can ask for a refund: see subsidies.json gb-ihs-reimbursement-eu.

items.title: Healthcare for stays of 6 months or less (EHIC)
items.title_it: Sanità per soggiorni fino a 6 mesi (TEAM/EHIC)

other: Without EUSS status

items.summary: For stays of 6 months or less no IHS is paid. A valid EHIC covers medically necessary treatment during the stay, but the UK government still advises buying travel/health insurance. Without cover, NHS hospital treatment for people who are not ordinarily resident can be charged at 150% of the NHS rate.
items.authority: Department of Health and Social Care / NHS England
items.notes: The NHS page notes that Icelandic, Liechtenstein and Swiss visitors may be charged and should check with their home authority. Rules read are for England; Scotland, Wales and NI pages were not opened.

items.title: Free NHS care with settled or pre-settled status
items.title_it: NHS gratuito con settled o pre-settled status

other: Holders of settled or pre-settled status, or with a pending EUSS application (certificate of application)

items.summary: EU citizens living in the UK after 30 June 2021 get free NHS healthcare only if they have settled or pre-settled status, or proof of a pending application. Free hospital treatment depends on being 'ordinarily resident'.
items.authority: Department of Health and Social Care

items.title: Registering with a GP (family doctor) in England
items.title_it: Registrarsi da un medico di base (GP) in Inghilterra
items.summary: Anyone in England, including temporary visitors from abroad, can register with a GP surgery for free. You do not need ID, proof of address or proof of immigration status, although a surgery may ask for documents in some cases.
items.notes: England only. Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have their own NHS bodies; their GP rules were not checked.

items.title: Opening a bank account
items.title_it: Aprire un conto in banca
items.summary: No official page on opening a bank account as a foreign student could be read. Ask your university's international student office which documents UK banks accept.
items.authority: UK Council for International Student Affairs (UKCISA) / university
items.notes: UKCISA, MoneyHelper and university pages returned 403/404 on 2026-11-25.

items.title: 16-25 Railcard
items.title_it: 16-25 Railcard (sconto treni)

other: Mature students 26+ in full-time education can apply with a form endorsed by their university

items.summary: Rail discount card for 16-25 year olds valid across Great Britain. Buy it online; the 1-year card can be bought up to the day before your 26th birthday, the 3-year card up to the day before your 24th.

items.title: Scotland: National Entitlement Card for free bus travel (under 22)
items.title_it: Scozia: National Entitlement Card per bus gratis (under 22)

other: Whether international/EU students living in Scotland during studies qualify is not stated on the page

items.summary: Under-22s who live in Scotland get free bus travel with a National Entitlement Card (or Young Scot NEC). Apply online at getyournec.scot (up to 10 working days) or through your council, with ID, proof of address and a photo. A university matriculation card is not valid for free travel.
items.notes: For international students, ask Transport Scotland (concessionarytravel@transport.gov.scot) or the local council.

items.title: Working on a Student visa
items.title_it: Lavorare con lo Student visa

other: Student visa holders on a full-time course with a university sponsor
Part-time postgraduates and students at private providers/pathway colleges generally may not work

items.summary: Degree-level students can work up to 20 hours a week in term time (10 hours below degree level) and full-time outside term time. Self-employment, business activity, professional sport/coaching, work as an entertainer and permanent full-time jobs are not allowed. Always check the conditions on your own visa.
items.notes: The gov.uk page does not state the hour limits; the 20/10 hours come from UKCISA (independent advisory body). Term time = the periods your university expects you to study.

items.title: Working with EUSS status or as an Irish citizen
items.title_it: Lavorare con EUSS status o da cittadino irlandese

other: Holders of settled or pre-settled status, or Irish citizens

items.summary: Settled/pre-settled status holders and Irish citizens can work in the UK without the hour limits of the Student visa; Irish citizens can also be self-employed.
items.notes: Working can stop an EU student from claiming the IHS refund (subsidies.json gb-ihs-reimbursement-eu).

items.title: No work as a Standard Visitor
items.title_it: Nessun lavoro come Standard Visitor
items.summary: Visitors (including those studying a short course on an ETA) cannot do paid or unpaid work for a UK company or as self-employed, except permitted paid engagements.

items.title: National Living Wage and National Minimum Wage (from April 2026)
items.title_it: Salario minimo legale (da aprile 2026)
items.summary: Hourly legal minimum, same across the UK: £12.71 at 21 and over (National Living Wage), £10.85 at 18-20, £8.00 under 18 and for apprentices. Valid from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027.
items.authority: HM Government (Department for Business and Trade / HMRC enforcement)

items.title: National Living Wage and National Minimum Wage (from April 2027)
items.title_it: Salario minimo legale (da aprile 2027)
items.summary: Rates published for 1 April 2027: £13.21 at 21 and over, £11.27 at 18-20, £8.31 under 18 and for apprentices.
items.authority: HM Government (Department for Business and Trade / HMRC enforcement)
items.notes: Apprentice rate applies to apprentices under 19 or in the first year of the apprenticeship.
